resources.title: Resources
resources.lead: Browse audio, video, PDFs and visual messages. No account needed.
explore_lead: Explore the five Hosn el Hal pillars, each offering simple, practical resources to support your wellbeing in different ways. From understanding your emotions and caring for yourself, to connecting with others and finding meaning in everyday moments, each pillar brings together videos, audios, visual messages and PDFs for you to explore.
There's no right place to start. Choose what feels most relevant to you today, and explore at your own pace.

pillars.psychoeducation: Build understanding about mental health and wellbeing, and explore what helps us feel and cope better.
pillars.self-awareness: Notice and understand our thoughts, feelings, body sensations and behaviours with kindness and curiosity.
pillars.realistic-self-care: Explore simple and realistic ways to take care of ourselves in daily life, even in challenging times.
pillars.peer-support: Explore how we can support and connect with each other, listen with care, and create safer, more supportive spaces.
pillars.reconnecting-with-purpose: Reconnect with what matters to us, explore our strengths, and find small ways to bring meaning into everyday life.

how_to_use.title: How to Use Hosn el Hal
how_to_use.lead: Hosn el Hal is flexible. There is no required sequence and no standalone training needed. Resources can be used independently or combined.
how_to_use.step_find_text: Search or filter by topic, format, length and language.
how_to_use.step_open_text: Watch videos, listen to audio, and view visual messages or PDFs in your browser.

how_to_use.practical_text: Use a resource on your own, with a small group of colleagues, or with the wider school team. The short notes with each resource provide practical suggestions.

about.title: Taking time for teachers’ wellbeing
about.name_text: Hosn el Hal is Arabic for wellness
about.lead: In emergencies, teachers are often deeply affected by the crisis, and yet we ask so much of them in supporting children to return safely to the classroom. Hosn el Hal offers dedicated, accessible mental health and psychosocial support resources for teachers as they support children during and after emergencies.

why.title: Teachers care for children through crisis. Their wellbeing matters too.
body: There is ample evidence that after an emergency, one of the most stabilising and healing experiences for children is returning to the routines and opportunities of a learning environment. Regular, predictable and nurturing care from teachers and education staff helps children feel safe to express and process distressing and potentially traumatic experiences.
Yet until now, too little attention has been paid to the mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of the adults who create these spaces for children.

Teachers’ wellbeing is essential for nurturing, responsive care. Workplace stress, burnout, compassion fatigue and exhaustion affect the quality of the support they can give. If they are not addressed, they can lead to long-term challenges such as students dropping out, difficulty keeping teachers and lower learning outcomes.

Studies show that when educators and facilitators take part in training and receive ongoing support to build their mental health literacy, they are better able to support their students’ mental health and psychosocial wellbeing. This can improve students’ outcomes in many areas, particularly learning and self-confidence.
why.aside_title: Teachers are part of the affected community
aside_items: They may have their own traumatic experiences of the emergency.
They are often caring for their own children and families.
They often face the same deprivation, grief, loss, fears and concerns as the children in their care.

how.title: A regional partnership
body: In response to multiple ongoing and compounding crises in the region, an inter-agency group of education and mental health specialists came together in Amman to share what we had, what we knew, and what we could do, to support teacher mental health and psychosocial wellbeing. Accessibility was key – how could we reach teachers within their busy schedules? How could we sustain engagement with shrinking budgets? How could we do better, together?

UNICEF convened practitioners from the Norwegian Refugee Council, Save the Children, UNRWA, and War Child who generously gave their insights, experiences, and resources which were distilled into the Hosn el Hal pillars and concept. Over the next year, UNRWA staff and teachers from Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine and Syria shared their ideas and reactions to designs and drafts, while expert feedback from each agency further improved and refined the assets.

The result is a series of resources that carry our original intent – to be used, to be shared, to be owned by anyone who is in a place to help teachers feel appreciated and supported. We hope that Hosn el Hal will help you do that.

different.title: What makes Hosn el Hal different

items.title: It complements what already exists
items.text: Hosn el Hal does not duplicate or replace existing approaches or packages. It offers complementary support that can be reached through alternative, innovative channels. This matters most in acute emergencies, where access barriers can limit the impact of more traditional programmes.

items.title: It builds on what we know works in the region
items.text: We gathered lessons learned from education and mental health resources already developed in the region. This helped us move quickly to create content that is effective, acceptable and speaks to teachers’ own needs.

items.title: It is designed to be accessible
items.text: Teachers are hard to reach for long, in-person training, and chronic stress affects how adults learn. So the content is easy to take in, strengths-based and inviting. It uses mixed media to suit different learning styles and time the teachers might have.

items.title: Teachers experience it first, then share it
items.text: Teachers are central to children’s emotional recovery. It works best when they benefit from this support themselves and then model it for students and bring it into their own teaching.

design.title: About our design
theme_body: A design rooted in the shared landscape of Syria, Jordan, Lebanon and Palestine, where earth tones convey stability, warmth and a sense of place. The composition reflects balance and structure: a steady ground to stand on. Subtle olive-inspired elements emerge within this foundation, evoking resilience, connection and community. Not about pushing through, but about finding your footing, together.
design.palette_alt: The Hosn el Hal colours on linen with olive leaves: olive green (#6B7F4A), silver sage (#A8B5A0), warm earth (#9C7C5C), terracotta (#C4704D) and warm sand (#EBDCC4).
logo_body: The Hosn el Hal logo draws from the architectural poetry of regional tilework, where repetition and geometry create quiet beauty. Built on a grid, the design reflects balance, structure and a sense of stability: a steady ground to stand on.

Within this foundation, a circular olive branch appears, gently connecting the four tiles. The form introduces a layer of movement and continuity, symbolising resilience, growth and the strength of community. The olives, positioned in a continuous loop, evoke connection: individuals held together within a shared space.

The interplay between structure and organic form creates a visual language that feels both grounded and alive. In this way, the identity brings together clarity and care, translating cultural familiarity into a sense of calm, connection and collective wellbeing.
design.logo_alt: The Hosn el Hal logo mark: four tiles in terracotta, olive green, sand and earth brown, joined by a circular olive branch

hub.title: A simple, accessible space
hub.text: This hub brings all Hosn el Hal resources together in one place: short videos, audio, visual messages and PDFs. There is no required sequence and no need to complete everything. Explore the resources, choose what feels useful to you, and return whenever you need a moment for your own wellbeing.

support_note.title: When you need more support
support_note.lead: Hosn el Hal can help you pause and care for yourself, and sometimes more support is needed too.
body: We all go through difficult moments, and sometimes we need a little more support to get through them. That's okay.

Hosn el Hal offers simple moments to pause, reconnect with yourself, and care for your wellbeing. While these resources can be helpful, they are not a replacement for professional mental health and psychosocial support.

If things are feeling particularly difficult, or if your feelings are making everyday life harder, please remember that you don't have to go through it alone. Reaching out to someone you trust, a school counsellor, a supervisor, or a support service available through your organisation can be an important first step.

If you're worried about someone else, whether a student or a colleague, sometimes the most helpful thing you can do is listen calmly, with care and without judgement. You don't need to have all the answers. Avoid investigating or promising to keep things secret, and follow your organisation's referral procedures to help connect them with the right support. If someone is at immediate risk of harm, follow your organisation's protection or emergency procedures right away.
Remember, caring for your wellbeing also means knowing when to reach out for support.
